title: 2005 HMMT February Team Round 2 Problem 2
statement: What are the dimensions of the rectangle of smallest area that is \((a, b)\)-tileable?

solutions.text:
If \(a=0\), then a \(1 \times 2 b\) rectangle is tileable in an obvious way. If \(a>0\), then a \(2 a \times 2 b\) rectangle is tileable by dividing the rectangle into quarters and pairing each square with a square from the diagonally opposite quarter. The answer is therefore \(\max \{1,2 a\} \times 2 b\). Minimality of area follows from the next question.
